scores.evidence: Phase 1 Foundation → Phase 2 Infrastructure → Phase 3 Build → Phase 4 Deployment
scores.rationale: Broad substrate-upward order exists, but nothing is proven before the next phase, and observability and security come late (Phases 6–7) after the deployment work that depends on them.

scores.evidence: Start with 5-10 pilot services, expand gradually
scores.rationale: The first 3 phases are planning and infrastructure, with no thin end-to-end production slice. The pilot line sits only in the risk table.
Tool choices are listed as options with no defaults, no flip conditions, and no irreversible-decision gate; the mono-repo vs. multi-repo choice is left open.

scores.evidence: Load test with realistic pipeline volume early
scores.rationale: There is a loose ordering from core infrastructure to pipelines, but no explicit blast-radius reasoning. Service mesh and canary work come before the leaf-level items with no stated rationale.

scores.evidence: Security review at each phase, penetration testing
scores.rationale: Image scanning appears in Phase 2 and SAST in Phase 3, but most security work is in a late Phase 7, and the per-phase review is only one risk-table line.
Observability is deferred to Phase 6, after deployment, with nothing in Phase 0 or the early phases.

scores.evidence: Auto-tag images with commit hash + build number
scores.rationale: Templates, versioned artifacts, GitOps with ArgoCD and repo templates give partial reproducibility, but there is no threading across phases and no environment-as-code statement.
Rollback and canary appear in Phase 4, and chaos testing in Phase 5. HA and DR are left to Phase 8, so resilience is not threaded from the start.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so there is no explicit N/A declaration.

scores.evidence: Add new microservices gradually; Migrate legacy services into platform
scores.rationale: Phase 10 names some later work and the risk table says to expand from a pilot, but there are no pull-forward conditions.

note: This is a generic waterfall-style checklist. It has no walking skeleton, no decision gates, and security, observability and resilience come late. It never addresses the AI question.
